findings.title: An empty hint line is 4px x 0, not 0x0: the hint rule's border-left-width overrides .message:empty
findings.evidence: `.message:empty { position: absolute; padding: 0; border-width: 0; }` (line 380) and `.message[data-message='hint'] { border-left-width: 4px; ... }` (line 397) have the same specificity (0,2,0). The hint rule comes later, so it wins, and an empty hint keeps a 4px left border. design.md decision 6 says the empty lines 'leave the flow instead (position: absolute, no padding or border, so 0×0)'. Nothing shows today because the box has zero height and a transparent border colour. But the claim is false for the hint line, and the hint line is not in the geometry selectors, so the e2e check cannot catch it.
findings.suggestion: Scope the hint border to non-empty lines (`.message[data-message='hint']:not(:empty)`), or move `.message:empty` after the hint rule. Alternatively, reword decision 6 so it does not claim 0x0 for the hint line.
verifierNotes: Confirmed in src/ui/style.css. `.message:empty` (line 380) and `.message[data-message='hint']` (line 397) both have specificity (0,2,0), and the hint rule comes later. It therefore overrides `border-width: 0` with `border-left-width: 4px` on an empty hint line. The empty hint is absolutely positioned with padding 0, so its width shrinks to fit and is 4px from the left border. Its height is 0. The box is 4px x 0, not the 0x0 that design decision 6 claims. The visible effect is nil, because the height is zero and the border is transparent, so the severity stays minor. The suggested fix of scoping the hint border to `:not(:empty)` or reordering the rules is correct.

In src/ui/style.css, `.message:empty` (line 380) and `.message[data-message='hint']` (line 397) both have specificity (0,2,0). The hint rule comes later, so its `border-left-width: 4px` overrides `border-width: 0`. `.message` already sets `border-style: solid` (line 370), so an empty hint keeps a 4px left border and its box is 4px x 0, contradicting the 0x0 claim in design decision 6. The win line has no such override and is unaffected. The effect is not visible (zero height, transparent border), so the minor severity is right. I did not check whether the e2e geometry selectors include the hint line.

findings.title: The --column formula repeats the 6x6 gap and padding as literals, and the #app copies of --board-gap/--board-pad are never read
findings.evidence: `--column: max(26rem, calc(6 * clamp(...) + 5 * 0.25rem + 2 * 0.375rem + 2px))` is written out at line 890 and again at line 919. It repeats the 6x6 `--board-gap: 0.25rem` / `--board-pad: 0.375rem` that `.board` declares at lines 171-172. `#app` also declares `--board-gap`/`--board-pad` (lines 78-79), but `.board` always sets its own, so nothing reads the #app copies. If the 6x6 gap or padding changes, the column silently stops matching the 6x6 board width.
findings.suggestion: Delete the #app copies. In #app, add named 6x6 variables (for example `--board6-gap`/`--board6-pad`) and use them in both --column formulas and in the .board default, or at least add a comment that ties the literals to the .board values.
verifierNotes: The mechanism is real. Lines 890 and 919 hardcode `5 * 0.25rem + 2 * 0.375rem + 2px`, which are the 6x6 defaults `.board` declares at lines 171-172. The only var(--board-gap/--board-pad) reads are at lines 173, 177 and 181, all inside `.board`, which always declares its own values, so the #app copies at lines 78-79 are dead. No TS code reads them either. If the 6x6 gap or padding changed, --column would silently drift from the board width. This is a maintainability and duplication issue, not a current wrong output, so the severity is minor and I downgrade it.

The facts check out in src/ui/style.css. The --column formula repeats the literals 5 * 0.25rem + 2 * 0.375rem + 2px at lines 890 and 919. Those match the .board defaults at lines 171-172 (--board-gap: 0.25rem, --board-pad: 0.375rem). #app declares --board-gap and --board-pad at lines 78-79, but .board always redeclares both (line 171), so descendants never inherit the #app values. Nothing reads the #app copies. The 6x6 board width is a separate formula at line 173, and --column is a second hand-synced copy of it. This is a latent maintenance coupling, not a live bug. Today the values agree, so no user sees a wrong result. It would only show up if someone edited the 6x6 gap or padding in one place and not the others. The other size-specific overrides (lines 195-218) apply to other sizes and do not affect the 6x6 column formula. The finding's own claim is only that the column would silently stop matching, which is true but needs a future edit. I downgrade it to a nit.

findings.title: The freeze script's provenance does not identify the build it measures
findings.evidence: The boxes are measured from `design/v0/out` (the build output). The provenance records `designCssSha1` of the source `design/v0/app/binarka.css` (line 84) and `git log -1 -- design/v0` (line 88). If `out/` is stale (built before the last CSS edit), the fixture records the new source hash next to geometry measured from the old build, and nothing reports the mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Hash the CSS that `design/v0/out` actually ships (or record the mtime or hash of the out bundle). Alternatively, fail when any file under design/v0/app is newer than design/v0/out/index.html.
verifierNotes: Confirmed at scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs. Boxes are measured from the gitignored build output design/v0/out. The provenance hashes the source design/v0/app/binarka.css and records the last git commit touching design/v0. The script only checks that out/index.html exists. It never compares the build with the source, by mtime or by hash. A stale out/ would therefore get the current source hash recorded next to geometry measured from the old build, and nothing would report the mismatch. The hash also covers only binarka.css, not components or other sources that affect layout. The impact is low because this is a manual, non-gate freeze script, so the finding stays minor.

Confirmed by reading scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs. Boxes are measured from the served design/v0/out (root at line ~41). Provenance hashes the source design/v0/app/binarka.css (line 84) and uses git log on design/v0 (line 88), not the built output. design/v0/out is gitignored (git check-ignore confirmed), so it is a local build that can be stale. The script only checks that index.html exists and has no freshness or mtime check. findings.title: Dev-only static server in freeze script decodes the URL path and joins it without a root check (path traversal)
findings.evidence: The server does join(root, decodeURIComponent(pathname)) and then readFileSync. `new URL()` normalises plain `../`, but a request with encoded dot-segments or a path that resolves outside design/v0/out after decoding (for example `%2e%2e%2f` combined with an encoded slash) can reach files outside the root. It binds to 127.0.0.1 and runs for seconds on a developer machine, so only a local process or a malicious page that can reach localhost:4177 could exploit it. It is not shipped code.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the path and reject it unless it starts with the resolved root plus a path separator. A static file server such as `sirv` or `vite preview` would also do, but AGENTS.md requires asking before adding a dependency.
verifierNotes: The mechanism holds. In scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs the server runs join(root, decodeURIComponent(new URL(req.url, 'http://x').pathname)) and then readFileSync. There is no check that the result stays under the root. I ran the same expression in Node. A request for `/..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd` keeps its `..%2f` segments through URL parsing, because the URL parser does not treat %2f as a separator. After decodeURIComponent the path is `/../../../etc/passwd`, and join() resolves it outside design/v0/out. With fewer `..%2f` segments it lands in other files in the repo. The finding's literal `%2e%2e%2f` example is partly wrong. URL parsing normalizes a bare `%2e%2e/` segment, so that form stays inside the root. The `..%2f` form is what escapes. The server binds only to 127.0.0.1, runs for a few seconds, and is dev-only. That is why the severity is minor.

The mechanism is real. In scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs (about lines 49-58) the server does join(root, decodeURIComponent(new URL(req.url,'http://x').pathname)) and there is no root check. I ran the path logic in node. A request for `/..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd` is not normalised by `new URL`, because the encoded slash hides the dot segments, so the pathname stays `/..%2f..%2f..%2fetc/passwd`. After decodeURIComponent, join() resolves it to `etc/passwd`, which is outside design/v0/out. Plain `%2e%2e/` is normalised by URL, so the finding's wording on that is imprecise, but the encoded-slash variant works. Exploitability is very limited. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 and runs only for the few seconds of a dev freeze script. A local process could read those files directly anyway. A malicious web page could send the request, but it could not read the response cross-origin because the server sends no CORS headers. The finding is therefore a valid but minor, dev-only hardening issue, and I am keeping its severity as is.
